gen-irish-grover-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads as a plain sans with a big x-height and curves that open wide at both ends, with no thick-thin shifts. Irish Grover is the chunky, soft-edged one up top, while Fira just gets on with the text.
gen-dafont-visitor-satoshi: Pixel-era charm meets a modern workhorse: Visitor has gaping-mouthed e shapes and short ascenders over big bowls, while Satoshi towers with a soaring x-height. Both keep their strokes drawn thin and uniform.
gen-dafont-woodgod-work-sans: Woodgod has a vintage, commanding look, with tall lowercase letters that nearly reach the capitals and a wide channel into every bowl. Work Sans takes over with a high mean line and sturdy joins, a modern sans-serif that keeps the page contemporary.
gen-flavors-manrope: Whimsical and a bit stubby, Flavors stacks a towering x-height over diagonals as hefty as its stems. Manrope follows with a bright gap at every curve, so a sans-serif body feels light by comparison.
gen-gf-autour-one-general-sans: Expressive and bold, Autour One has round letters with a clear channel leading in and almost no step from capital to lowercase. And General Sans fills the line with a tall x-height and smooth bends, a sans that stays out of its way.
gen-gf-goldman-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, a sans-serif that reads with quiet authority. Goldman sits wide and commanding beside it, with round forms like open parentheses and a big lowercase that makes the two feel related.
gen-gf-grandstander-fs-supreme: Chunky and playful, Grandstander has short ascenders, a tall x-height and simple lines drawn as if with one tip. Its strongest quality is how open both fonts stay, with Supreme carrying a thick, heavy strip of sans text.
gen-gf-gugi-montserrat: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly reaches its capitals, and its terminals are cut open so counters flow outward. Montserrat brings the white space and oversized e and a counters that let a sans-serif line glide.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-switzer: Expressive is the word for Love Ya Like A Sister, with ascenders barely clearing the x-height and terminal tips pointing outward. Switzer does its best work in tubular, wire-like letters with a tall waist line, a plain sans that keeps the pair steady.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-ranade: Ranade moves with a spread-out line of widely spaced type, its weight shifting only slightly like stretched rubber cord. And if Origami, with its single-stroke brush look and lowercase like poured lead, is made small, that mass loses its punch.
